text: In 1997, the ocean made a sound no one could explain.
Underwater microphones, built to hunt submarines, picked it up.
It was so loud, sensors almost five thousand kilometres apart heard it.
It came from one of the most remote places on Earth. Deep in the South Pacific.
Its shape looked like an animal's call. They named it... the Bloop.
But it was far louder than a blue whale. The loudest animal we know.
So what is bigger than a blue whale?
For years, nobody knew. And the internet decided it was a monster.
Then, in 2005, scientists found the answer.
It was ice. A giant iceberg, cracking and breaking apart, off Antarctica.
The scariest sound in the ocean... was the planet, breaking.
